items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: I'd get Art Blakey, or I'd get Kenny Clark or I'd get Max Roach, you know, because they were in there all the time anyway.

ctx.x: A frightening band. Bird and Diz in the same band.
Yeah. Well, I will say this for Billy Ekstine, he really, really tried to help Sarah. I mean from his heart and all the guys, and Diz and Bird, and all the guys, you know and Kenny Clark

you know he was married to Carmen McRae at the time, but everybody got together. They wanted to make it, you know what I mean. And she was just a regular, you know, so she had the talent and she come out of church in Jersey and a choir and she had all the equipment and the main thing is she knew the keyboard, and that's a tremendous help because you can check yourself out anytime, you don't have to depend on bringing somebody in to check you out, you know what I mean, rehearsal. You rehearse yourself. Hahahaha.…

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: And of course Kenny Clarke and Monk and, let's see, Eddie Davis was around there at the time and then he eventually became house band there.

ctx.x: Do you remember the first day you came to the City...how you came and who you were with?
We came in on a bus and I went and stayed at that hotel right next to Minton's,

what is the name of that hotel? Anyway, all the musicians stayed there and anyway I went right into the hotel, then Minton's was right downstairs. And that was just right for me. Boy oh boy, I'd come downstairs every night and Lester Young would be blowin' and Harold ("Doc") West and, oh gee whiz, Don Byas and I got a chance to really hear all these wonderful people and see them in this New York setting, you know what I mean, and it was just wonderful. And of course Kenny Clarke and Monk and, let's see, Eddie…
